units.unit: Needs sources for an essay on Hong Kong rent control for subdivided units
Wants the source documenting the per-square-foot premium SDU tenants pay
The source must stand as evidence for a claim already being made: SDU tenants pay a 15–25 percent per-square-foot premium
The premium is the anchor for why tightening looks intuitive before counter-arguments
Wants the primer source for the 15-25 percent premium anchor
Wants the primer source for the queue length
D1p1 gives the per-square-foot premium SDU tenants pay
D1p2 gives the five-and-a-half-year public housing queue
D1p3 shows the 2021 ordinance was second-generation, capping increases within a tenancy but leaving initial rents untouched
The second-generation point is the hinge of the argument: stable SDU stock shows only that moderate, non-binding regulation is survivable, not that a hard initial-rent cap is safe
Wants the companion data piece on the current SDU stock trend
Wants the think-tank note on the floor-standard-plus-rent-band proposal
Needs the actual stock trend — the 2019 figure and the latest figure — stated precisely
The stable stock is the only hard evidence that the ordinance didn't shrink the segment
Wants the think-tank's own characterization of why the stock stayed stable
If the think-tank calls the stability an artifact of a non-binding instrument, that counters reading flat stock as proof a hard cap is safe
All five sources are cited by the essay and each carries a passage still unread
All five cited, each carries an unread passage still needed
All cited, all carry unread passages needed
Still needs D3, the tenant case notes on Mr Chan
Still needs D4, the NGO tenant interviews with Mrs Wong
Still needs D5, the landlord association statement
Still needs D9, the legal opinion on compensation and judicial review
Still needs D10, the enforcement capacity and tenancy register study
D3 is the tenant case notes on Mr Chan
Cited passage: his two-week eviction after requesting a window repair
Cited passage: the subcommittee's inability to find a design protecting the newest-arrival tail first
Cited passage: his own preference for the waiting list over a hard cap
Cited passage: the legal-exposure point about compensation and judicial review
Mr Chan is the case-study hinge: the tenant actually harmed says the waiting list, not a rent cap, is what would let him leave
Needs D3p1 for the eviction trigger (two weeks after a repair request)
Needs D3p3 for his stated preference
Needs D3p2 for the subcommittee's point that no design protects the newest-arrival tail first
Needs D3p4 for the compensation/judicial-review exposure
Wants the three remaining sources the argument leans on
